extraction_method: Reproduced the 20260903 scrape method: same private JSON API (POST /api/leaderboard {arenaType, category, variationName, inputModality?}; GET /api/leaderboard/judge-scores; POST /api/leaderboard/llm-scores; GET /api/registry) on https://www.designarena.ai/leaderboard. This browser session is shared by nine other rescrape agents, each in its own isolated chrome-devtools context. A dedicated page was opened at pageId 21 (isolatedContext=design-arena-rescrape-20260904; an earlier page opened under a differently-named context was closed and superseded per a coordinator instruction mid-task). Page-selection races were severe and bidirectional in this run: three separate select_page->evaluate_script or select_page->navigate_page pairs landed on other agents' pages instead of the intended one (evidenced by the returned location.href belonging to deepswe.datacurve.ai, epoch.ai, and -- worst -- a navigate_page call that changed another agent's page (isolatedContext=artificial-analysis-rescrape-20260904, later also briefly vals-ai-rescrape-20260904) to designarena.ai/leaderboard/android). Both accidental hijacks were caught immediately via the returned href/isolatedContext mismatch and reverted by navigating the affected page back to its original URL (artificialanalysis.ai/leaderboards/models). No pages that this agent did not open were closed. Because of the high collision rate, browser use was limited to one successful cross-check fetch (models/allcategories via evaluate_script on the confirmed designarena.ai page returned count=162 with modelId kimi-k3 elo=1396, matching the shape and near-identical live values of the later Node fetch) plus reconnaissance of the site's footer nav links and one page's __NEXT_DATA__/HTML to hunt for new categories. The full 33-endpoint sweep (32 leaderboard categories + llm-scores, plus judge-scores and registry) was then executed via Node fetch in Bash, consistent with the fallback already accepted in the 20260903 meta.json.
notes: raw.json holds untouched API payloads keyed by "<arenaType>/<category>[/<inputModality>]", plus the full /api/registry (model display names, providers, pricing) and the judge-scores / llm-scores payloads.

Elo is the site metric; battles map to votes; winRate is a percentage (0-100). btStdErr is the Bradley-Terry standard error the API returns (frequently null in today's payloads, passed through as-is, not fabricated).
inputModality variants are distinct site leaderboards: models/website/image = Image-to-HTML, models/website/video = Video-to-Website, agents/agon_webapps/image = Image-to-Webapp.

cost_usd is not published as a single number by the site; the registry gives per-1M-token text pricing, emitted as cost_usd_input_per_1m_tokens / cost_usd_output_per_1m_tokens only where present. Nothing blended or estimated.
context_window is not exposed anywhere on the site, so it is omitted from every record.
date is the per-category metadata.lastUpdateTime returned by the API.

Category-discovery sweep: the site's footer nav (37 links) and the /leaderboard/android page's embedded route/i18n data were checked for categories added since 20260903. Every link mapped onto one of the already-known 32 categories (e.g. /leaderboard/android is the existing agents/nativeapps category's page, not a new one -- confirmed against the 20260903 normalized.json source_url mapping). No new category was found. The 7 categories that returned an empty data array on 20260903 (models/music, models/sts, models/worldmodel, agents/agon_dataviz, agents/agentic_3d, agents/fullstack_gamedev, agents/agon_html) were re-checked today and are still empty.

Category ids "imagetohtml" and "videotowebsite" appear in the client bundle but are rejected by the API (400 Invalid category); those pages are the website category with an inputModality filter, which is what was captured.
Only variationName "public" appears in the client code; no other variation was requested.
No login, no voting, no CAPTCHA; nothing was blocked.
